answer: An agent lending market for orchard and grove equipment grants no unsecured signup credit. Every 100-coin loan requires 150 coins of collateral in a contract vault; the ledger reserves that collateral for this loan alone until repayment. Ten aliases borrowing 100 each must therefore tie up 1,500 coins, rather than reuse one deposit ten times. Default liquidates the reserved assets even if the borrower abandons its key. This blocks free credit multiplication, assuming conservative valuation and a price oracle the borrower cannot manipulate.
